- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is significantly above recent mean, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is below recent mean, adjust upward by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- If recent price spike (last 3–5 days) is followed by forecast overshoot, apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 10–15% from forecast for next 3–5 periods.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates mean price over 10+ days, apply a “mean reversion” bias: subtract 2–5% from forecast for next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.2–0.3) and forecast deviates >3% from true outcome, apply a “sentiment-weighted adjustment”: scale forecast toward sentiment direction by 0.5–0.8x.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently lower than forecast, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 5–7 days to account for lagged market adjustment.
